subject: Business Models
title: B2B Marketplaces
description: A quick win: understand B2B Marketplaces.

hook.text: Alibaba connects factories directly to businesses worldwide. B2B marketplaces handle $7.7 trillion in trade.

buildup.text: B2B marketplaces digitize procurement: finding suppliers, comparing quotes, managing orders at scale.

discovery.text: B2B transactions are larger and stickier. Once a factory relationship is established, switching is painful.

twist.text: B2B marketplaces are 10 years behind B2C. Most industrial procurement still happens via phone, fax, and email.

climax.text: The $7.7 trillion B2B marketplace opportunity dwarfs consumer e-commerce. Digitization is just beginning.

punchline.text: $7.7 trillion, still on fax machines. B2B is the next frontier.

quiz.question: Why are B2B marketplace relationships sticky?
options: Switching factory relationships is costly and painful

details.summary: B2B marketplaces connect businesses with suppliers, manufacturers, and service providers, handling transactions that are typically larger, more complex, and involve longer decision cycles than consumer marketplaces..
details.whyItMatters: B2B commerce is a 20 trillion dollar market that is far less digitized than consumer e-commerce. B2B marketplaces that solve procurement complexity, payment terms.
takeaways: B2B transactions are larger and more complex than consumer marketplace deals
Longer decision cycles involve multiple stakeholders and formal procurement processes
B2B commerce is far less digitized than consumer e-commerce, creating massive opportunity

faq.question: How do B2B marketplaces differ from consumer marketplaces?
faq.answer: B2B transactions involve higher values, longer cycles, negotiated pricing, payment terms of 30 to 90 days, multiple decision-makers, compliance requirements, and ongoing relationships rather than one-time purchases..

faq.question: What are the biggest challenges for B2B marketplace builders?
faq.answer: Complex purchasing workflows with multiple approvals. Payment terms requiring credit risk management. Custom pricing that resists marketplace standardization. Relationship-dependent sales that resist platform intermediation. Smaller buyer bases that make network effects harder to achieve.
